title: Survey: Most Microsoft India Staff Report Hikes Of Five Percent Or Less
excerpt: A Blind survey of 2,178 India-based professionals found 91% of Microsoft respondents reporting hikes of 5% or less — self-reported figures that arrive alongside a voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees.
body:
• In a Blind survey of 2,178 India-based tech professionals, 91% of Microsoft respondents said they received a hike of 5% or less this year, up from 45% last year.
  • Only 5% of Microsoft respondents reported a hike above 10%, down from 27%, and 86% said they were dissatisfied — the second-highest share after Zoho.
  • Blind is an anonymous workplace app and the figures are self-reported survey responses, not confirmed Microsoft policy; company results cover firms with at least 30 responses.
  • For employees weighing options: the survey coincides with Microsoft's voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees, with eligible staff reported to have until early December to decide.

Ninety-one percent of Microsoft respondents in India received a salary hike of 5% or less in this year's appraisal cycle, according to a survey by Blind, the anonymous community app for professionals — a sharp deterioration from 45% a year earlier. The findings, published by Blind and reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, are self-reported responses from 2,178 India-based professionals surveyed between October 15 and 26, 2026. They describe what respondents say they received, and should not be read as Microsoft's confirmed pay policy.

The Microsoft numbers in the survey

Only 5% of Microsoft respondents said they got a raise of more than 10%, down from 27% last year, and 86% said they were dissatisfied with their hike — the second-highest dissatisfaction share in the survey, after Zoho. At Zoho, founder Sridhar Vembu froze annual hikes this year, citing rising AI and server costs while saying the company would work to avoid mass layoffs; 95% of Zoho respondents reported no raise or a pay cut and 90% were dissatisfied. Microsoft's weak readings came from a company-level cut that Blind publishes only for companies with at least 30 responses per question, and the year-over-year comparison draws on 2,417 India-based respondents to Blind's 2025 survey.

A weak year across Indian tech

The Microsoft figures sit inside a broader squeeze. Across all respondents, 35% said they received no hike (30%) or took a pay cut (5%). Including those who got 1-5%, 59% received a hike of 5% or less, up from 34% in 2025. Overall, 63% were dissatisfied, including 47% who were very dissatisfied. No hike or a pay cut was most common at Oracle (60%), Salesforce (42%), Cisco (40%) and Amazon (36%), while Nutanix stood out at the other end, with 67% of its respondents receiving raises above 10%. Respondents largely blamed company decisions rather than their own ratings: 41% cited the company's financial performance or cost-cutting as the biggest factor, 18% pointed to AI and automation, and only 22% cited their individual performance rating.

Buyouts sharpen the anxiety

Blind said the small raises at Microsoft have coincided with buyouts. Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees across India, the U.S., Canada and the U.K. as it pours money into AI, according to Blind's report. Coverage of the offer reported by Archynewsy said Chief People Officer Amy Coleman detailed a Voluntary Exit Offer covering employees at level 70 and below, with eligible employees having until early December to decide. Search behaviour on Blind points the same way: over the past year, 21% of Blind users in India searched for layoffs or severance, up from 16% the year before, while the share searching for buyouts and voluntary exit programmes rose 60% and the share searching for hikes, raises or pay freezes fell 7%. For Indian tech workers, the survey captures a cycle in which pay growth has stalled at the same moment a large exit offer is on the table — a combination that explains why job security, rather than the hike itself, now dominates workplace conversation.
